claims.locator: Kentucky — 2026 TEMPORARY STATEHOUSE CONFIGURATION — HIGH PRIORITY
claims.statement:
Kentucky is a crucial example of why environment data must be year-versioned rather than permanently binding a role to a historic room.


Verified current condition:
- The Kentucky State Capitol closed beginning August 20, 2025 for a $291.5 million multiyear renovation, with reopening expected only after the renovation period.
- The Governor's office was relocated to 501 High Street, 2nd Floor, Frankfort.
- During the 2026 legislative session, House and Senate floor proceedings occur in a temporary structure near the east end of the Capitol Annex rather than in the historic Capitol chambers.
- Public viewing is routed through designated Annex rooms via livestream while the temporary chambers are in use.
- The Capitol Annex remains a major working legislative environment, including member/staff offices and committee rooms.


Scene families required for a 2026 start:
1. TEMPORARY HOUSE CHAMBER — functional temporary legislative hall; do not render the ornate historic House chamber.
2. TEMPORARY SENATE CHAMBER — same temporary-building family but chamber-specific seating/rostrum details.
3. CAPITOL ANNEX MEMBER OFFICE — actual working-office family for legislators/staff.
4. CAPITOL ANNEX COMMITTEE ROOM — multiple room variants, with real room numbers/capacities/layout references available from LRC.
5. TEMPORARY GOVERNOR WORKING OFFICE — 501 High Street office-building context, not the historic Capitol executive suite.
6. HISTORIC KENTUCKY CAPITOL — retained as a separate era/location family for pre-renovation starts and eventual post-renovation return, not used by default in 2026.


Design implication: a Kentucky political career begun in 2026 can later experience a genuine physical move back into the restored Capitol. That change can become canonical history, not merely a background swap.


Official sources:
https://www.kentucky.gov/Pages/Activity-stream.aspx?n=FinanceandAdministrationCabinet&prId=334
https://legislature.ky.gov/Visitors/Pages/default.aspx
https://legislature.ky.gov/LRC/Publications/Documents/Legislative%20Handbook.pdf


Reference status: BUILDING/USE VERIFIED. Dedicated visual photo packs still need to be assembled for the temporary chambers, representative Annex offices/committee rooms, 501 High Street interior, and historic chambers before final scene art.

Virginia now provides one of the clearest examples of why the game must time-version environments.
EXECUTIVE:
- Current official legislative/government material places the Governor and Cabinet secretaries in the Patrick Henry Building, 1111 East Broad Street, with Governor/Cabinet activity on the third floor.
- Current 2026 gubernatorial activity, including Cabinet meetings, uses the Patrick Henry Building.
- The building received a major 2025–26 interior refresh. Official project material describes a lighter natural palette inspired by Virginia geography ('Piedmont to Shore'), a redesigned lobby/reception experience, adjustable-height desks, sliding privacy doors, standardized modern breakrooms, upgraded audiovisual systems and furniture produced by Virginia Correctional Enterprises.
- Therefore a 2026 Patrick Henry executive scene should NOT reuse an older dark/traditional executive-office image merely because it is historically associated with Virginia government.
LEGISLATURE:
- The new General Assembly Building opened in 2023: fourteen stories above grade plus one below, a two-story lobby and large atrium, 11 subcommittee rooms, 8 large committee rooms (largest roughly 392 seats), member/staff offices, café/coffee facilities and tunnel connections to the Capitol/parking. The modern-classical building incorporates the preserved 1912 facade.
- The historic Capitol remains the chamber/ceremonial family; the General Assembly Building is the everyday office/committee family.
RESIDENCE/HISTORY:
- Executive Mansion is a separate residence/ceremonial environment.
- Historic 'Old Governor's Office' material must not be mistaken for the modern daily executive workspace; it has not been the primary working office for more than a century.
Production implication: Virginia should be a flagship test of the `architecture/building + era override + modular personal artifacts` pipeline.
Photo-pack status: STRONG / PRODUCTION-GRADE OFFICIAL SOURCE FAMILY AT BUILDING/ERA LEVEL. Exact room-by-room extraction still occurs before art production.

claims.locator: Tennessee — HISTORIC CAPITOL + MODERN CORDELL HULL SPLIT
claims.statement:
Tennessee's working legislature is physically split across two strongly different environment families.


Verified current condition:
- The historic Tennessee State Capitol remains the chamber/ceremonial core.
- Current House/Senate member offices, leadership staff, research staff, Office of Legal Services, Fiscal Review and numerous legislative administrative functions are located in the Cordell Hull Building.
- Official staff/directory records repeatedly place members and staff in numbered Cordell Hull Building rooms while the House Chief Clerk/Engrossing and selected chamber functions remain in the State Capitol.
- Current public meetings identify House Hearing Room II and other legislative hearing rooms inside Cordell Hull as active government meeting locations.


Scene families required:
1. TENNESSEE CAPITOL HOUSE CHAMBER.
2. TENNESSEE CAPITOL SENATE CHAMBER.
3. TENNESSEE CAPITOL CHIEF-CLERK/ENGROSSING/CHAMBER-SUPPORT family where official functions remain in the historic building.
4. CORDELL HULL MEMBER OFFICE family — modern working-office environment.
5. CORDELL HULL LEADERSHIP OFFICE variant where materially different.
6. CORDELL HULL HOUSE/SENATE HEARING ROOM family.
7. CORDELL HULL JOINT STAFF/LEGAL/FISCAL office family.
8. CONNECTING CORRIDOR/TUNNEL/transition context where gameplay needs movement between the buildings.


Design implication: a Tennessee legislator can leave an ornate historic floor session and return to a much more contemporary office/hearing-building environment. Do not make the office look like an extension of the historic chamber.


Official sources:
https://www.capitol.tn.gov/house/staff/
https://capitol.tn.gov/directory/
https://www.tn.gov/osa/calendar/2026/8/13/-state-building-commission-meeting.html


Reference status: USE/LOCATION VERIFIED. A dedicated contemporary Cordell Hull interior-photo pass remains required before art generation.

claims.locator: California — 1021 O Street legislative working-office family CONFIRMED
claims.statement:
Current Assembly member/committee pages and current Senate records repeatedly list Capitol offices/committee suites at 1021 O Street. This verifies 1021 O Street as a major 2026 Assembly and Senate working-office family during the Capitol Annex project, not merely a governor mailing/swing-space address. Some current offices can occupy other nearby state buildings, so assignment remains person/committee-specific.
Status: 2026 LEGISLATIVE WORKING FAMILY CONFIRMED; retain person/committee-level room assignment rather than assuming every member is in one building.

The State Office Building is closed for renovation, with return expected in 2027. Current 2025–26 House directories place House members and substantial House staff/research functions in the Centennial Office Building, 658 Cedar Street. Current Senate directories place senators in the Minnesota Senate Building.
Production implication: for 2026 scenes, House-member working offices should use the Centennial temporary family, Senate-member working offices the Minnesota Senate Building family, and the closed State Office Building should not appear as an occupied normal House office environment.
Status: 2026 ERA OVERRIDE RESOLVED AT BUILDING-FAMILY LEVEL.

claims.locator: Minnesota — THREE-BUILDING LEGISLATIVE COMPLEX + TEMPORARY CONSTRUCTION STATE
claims.statement:
Current official Legislature guidance distinguishes the Capitol, State Office Building and Minnesota Senate Building. This topology is time-sensitive: as of 2026 the State Office Building is temporarily closed for construction, altering public/House-space use.


Verified current spaces:
- Capitol public/meeting rooms on the third floor including 309A, 316, 317/317A/317B and Public Business Center 318.
- Capitol press conference room B971.
- Senate hearing rooms in the Minnesota Senate Building.
- Legislative Reference Library locations in the Capitol and Minnesota Senate Building.
- Public/security rules changed for the 2026 session, including screening at Capitol/Senate Building entrances and additional chamber-gallery screening.


Official source:
https://www.leg.mn.gov/leg/FAQ/faq?subject=14


Scene families:
1. MINNESOTA HOUSE CHAMBER.
2. MINNESOTA SENATE CHAMBER.
3. CAPITOL PUBLIC/COMMITTEE/CONFERENCE family.
4. CAPITOL PRESS ROOM B971.
5. MINNESOTA SENATE BUILDING HEARING-ROOM family.
6. MINNESOTA SENATE BUILDING office/circulation family.
7. STATE OFFICE BUILDING family with year-specific construction/closure status.
8. Security-screening/entry state as an environmental/access layer, not permanent architecture.


Hard rule: the selected year can change which building/room is available. Do not render the State Office Building as normal public House space in a 2026 scene without resolving its construction status.

claims.locator: Texas — HISTORIC CAPITOL + UNDERGROUND EXTENSION + SPLIT MEMBER OFFICES
claims.statement:
Texas requires multiple linked but visually distinct scene families.


Verified current condition:
- The Capitol remains an active historic government building with House and Senate chambers, Governor spaces and selected member offices.
- The official building directory distinguishes Governor's Public Reception Room, Press Conference space, Business Office and Legislative Division.
- The Governor's Public Reception Room is a functioning ceremonial room with historically restored/original furnishings including a marble-topped table, brass chandelier and S-shaped tête-à-tête sofa.
- The Governor's original first-floor private office is restored to approximately its c.1910 appearance but today is used by a senior staff member; the Governor offices on the second floor. This distinction prevents misusing a museum/historic room as the current working governor office.
- Current legislators are split between historic Capitol rooms and Capitol Extension rooms; the directory explicitly lists senators in both.
- The underground Capitol Extension provides office, committee/conference, auditorium and service spaces and is a separate modern-1990s environment family, not merely a basement texture of the historic Capitol.


Scene families required:
1. TEXAS HOUSE CHAMBER — restored historic family.
2. TEXAS SENATE CHAMBER — restored historic family.
3. GOVERNOR CURRENT WORKING-OFFICE family — distinguish from the restored original private office.
4. GOVERNOR PUBLIC RECEPTION ROOM — ceremonial/visitor context.
5. GOVERNOR PRESS-CONFERENCE room/context.
6. HISTORIC CAPITOL MEMBER OFFICE family.
7. CAPITOL EXTENSION MEMBER OFFICE family.
8. CAPITOL EXTENSION COMMITTEE/CONFERENCE family.
9. HISTORIC CORRIDOR/ROTUNDA family.
10. EXTENSION OPEN-AIR/ATRIUM circulation family where relevant.


Official sources:
https://tspb.texas.gov/plan/maps/doc/capitol_building_directory.pdf
https://tspb.texas.gov/prop/tc/tc-spaces/spaces03.html
https://tspb.texas.gov/prop/tc/tc-spaces/spaces14.html
https://tspb.texas.gov/PROP/TC/tc-spaces/spaces.html


Reference status: STRONG OFFICIAL VISUAL/ROOM SOURCE FAMILY, including State Preservation Board photospheres and significant-space galleries. Extension member-office/committee contemporary photo pack still needs deliberate collection.

claims.locator: New York — STRONG OFFICIAL CAPITOL/CHAMBER/MANSION PACK
claims.statement:
Official Empire State Plaza/Capitol virtual material provides room-specific identities.
- Senate Chamber: H. H. Richardson design, opened 1881, historically rich carved/ornamental treatment including a heavily decorated/gilded ceiling.
- Assembly Chamber: Leopold Eidlitz, Moorish Gothic visual family, materially different from the Senate rather than a recolor.
- Executive Mansion has a separate official virtual-visit/source family and must remain a residence/ceremonial environment distinct from Capitol working spaces.
- Current Assembly directories place most Albany member offices in the Legislative Office Building (LOB), with some Capitol assignments. Current governor schedules confirm active political use of rooms such as the State Capitol Red Room.
Production implication: at least four Albany families are necessary: Senate Chamber, Assembly Chamber, ceremonial/political Capitol rooms, and LOB working offices; Executive Mansion is a separate residence family.
Photo-pack status: STRONG CAPITOL/CHAMBER/MANSION BASE; LOB everyday office interiors still need a focused pack.

claims.locator: North Dakota — NAMED COMMITTEE-ROOM SYSTEM INSIDE THE CAPITOL
claims.statement:
North Dakota provides an unusually clear official room inventory. The Legislative Assembly uses named rooms across the ground floor/legislative wing and tower, including Prairie, Harvest, Roughrider, Red River, Sakakawea, Fort Lincoln, Fort Totten, Fort Union, Peace Garden and Brynhild Haugland Rooms. Current calendars/hearing records tie actual committees to these room names and occasionally to numbered rooms such as 216.


Official map/source:
https://ndlegis.gov/sites/default/files/resource/miscellaneous/capitolbuildingmap_1.pdf
https://ndlegis.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/committees/69-2025/27.5090.02000appendixh.pdf


Scene families:
1. NORTH DAKOTA HOUSE CHAMBER.
2. NORTH DAKOTA SENATE CHAMBER.
3. ROUGHRIDER ROOM.
4. PEACE GARDEN ROOM.
5. PIONEER ROOM.
6. HARVEST / RED RIVER / SAKAKAWEA named-room family, with room-specific references retained.
7. FORT LINCOLN / FORT TOTTEN / FORT UNION / BRYNHILD HAUGLAND legislative-wing family.
8. PRAIRIE ROOM tower family.
9. Capitol atrium/café/public circulation where gameplay uses it.


Production implication: these names are meaningful place identities. A calendar should say `Peace Garden Room`, not just `Committee Room B`.

Official OMB Capitol virtual-tour/photo-gallery resources cover Legislative Hall, House chamber, Senate chamber and other spaces and identify distinctive room-specific material/lighting language: Art Deco high-rise statehouse, House ceiling/light treatment associated with moon/stars, Senate English-oak/sunset treatment, rosewood/maple Legislative Hall, and other unusual rooms. Official directories also map Governor, legislative, press and committee functions by floor.
Photo-pack status: STRONG OFFICIAL SOURCE PACK.

Official Nebraska Capitol resources now provide unusually production-useful coverage of the Governor's Suite and legislative interiors. Governor-suite material distinguishes Hearing Room, Reception Area, Governor private office and Chief of Staff office, and describes Italian Renaissance treatment, walnut wainscoting, fireplaces, murals, carved agricultural/state motifs, decorative plaster, custom furnishings and the painted-dome private office. The Capitol Commission also provides Capitol photographs for free use, and the Legislature provides downloadable high-resolution interior photography including chamber and public-space sets.
Photo-pack status: STRONG OFFICIAL SOURCE PACK. Asset extraction/annotation remains future production work, but generic invention is no longer necessary.

claims.locator: New Mexico — ROUNDHOUSE ROOM-SPECIFIC COMMITTEE SYSTEM
claims.statement:
Current 2025 official committee schedules expose concrete Roundhouse room identities. Examples include House Appropriations & Finance in Room 307 and House Commerce & Economic Development in Room 317. The schedule also supports remote Zoom attendance, but the physical room remains the canonical meeting location.


Official source example:
https://www.nmlegis.gov/Agendas/Standing/hSched030825.pdf


Scene families:
1. NEW MEXICO HOUSE CHAMBER.
2. NEW MEXICO SENATE CHAMBER.
3. ROOM 307 appropriations/finance family.
4. ROOM 317 committee family.
5. other numbered Roundhouse hearing rooms after visual/photo reference collection.
6. Roundhouse rotunda/art/public circulation family.
7. Capitol North offices where the specific role/office is verified.


Production implication: preserve the Roundhouse's circular/art-rich architectural identity, but do not fill every room with generic Southwest decoration; permanent institutional art/architecture belongs in the base asset while occupant decoration remains modular.

Official Legislature visitor resources provide self-guided Capitol material, Legislature tour video and Capitol Art Tour; official handbook material establishes the circular/Zia geometry, multi-level rotunda/skylight, chambers, committee rooms and integrated art program.
Photo-pack status: PARTIAL -> STRONGER OFFICIAL BASE, exact scene-by-scene annotation pending.

Verified identity:
- Oldest congressional office building, opened 1908; Beaux-Arts institutional family.
- Original member offices averaged about 15 x 23 feet and were essentially single-room offices by later congressional standards.
- Original fittings included oak/mahogany furniture, meeting/storage/desk pieces, running water/sink, telephone, electric lighting and forced-air heat/ventilation.
- Current Cannon has undergone a decade-scale modernization/renewal while restoring historic architectural assets, so a contemporary Cannon room should not be rendered as an untouched 1908 museum set.


Base-art implication: compact historic-proportioned office with modernized infrastructure and inherited classical building fabric. Personal photographs/books/district objects belong to the modular occupant layer.


Official sources:
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/Cannon-Building/Cannon-Building/
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/Cannon-Building/Designed-for-the-Modern-Age/
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/Cannon-Building/Furnishing-the-Building/

Verified identity:
- 1933 neoclassical-revival building; smaller than Cannon/Rayburn in overall scale but with substantially more developed member suites than early Cannon.
- Each original member office suite consisted of a main greeting/staff room, private representative office and individual lavatory.
- Historic interior language included walnut paneling/furniture, colored carpet/curtains, marble corridors, bronze chandeliers and highly finished elevators.
- Large committee/assembly spaces have their own Colonial Revival/classical detailing.


Base-art implication: an interwar congressional suite with greeting-room + private-office spatial logic; not a generic modern rectangle and not as large/late-modern as Rayburn.


Official sources:
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/House-Office-Buildings/Longworth/Longworth-intro/
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/House-Office-Buildings/Longworth/Interior/
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/House-Office-Buildings/Longworth/Design/

Verified identity:
- Completed 1965; largest House office building and a distinctly postwar/mid-century expansion of congressional workspace.
- Planned member offices were four-chamber suites with selectable blue/beige schemes; building included extensive committee/subcommittee/staff space.
- The scale and suite organization reflect the much larger postwar congressional staff institution.


Base-art implication: larger mid-century congressional office suite with reception/staff/private-room separation, not a palette-swapped Longworth room.


Official source:
https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/House-Office-Buildings/Rayburn/Members_move/

Verified identity:
- First Senate office building, occupied 1909; richly classical historic family.
- Original senator suite consisted of two rooms, one for senator and one for personal staff; senator office included a fireplace and large exterior/courtyard window.
- Modern suites combine multiple earlier offices to accommodate contemporary staffs, so current Russell need not reproduce the exact original two-room footprint.
- Building includes the historic Caucus Room and a rotunda with Corinthian columns/coffered dome.


Base-art implication: classical/historic office family with large windows/fireplace-capable inherited rooms, modernized/combined into contemporary working suites.


Official source:
https://www.senate.gov/about/historic-buildings-spaces/office-buildings/russell-building.htm

Verified identity:
- Opened 1958 for the postwar/television-era Senate.
- Committee hearing rooms were deliberately designed as two-story, wood-paneled rooms with raised daises and broadcast facilities; private executive-meeting chambers and staff rooms adjoin them.
- This is an excellent real template for formal mid-century committee hearing scenes.


Base-art implication: functional mid-century Senate office/hearing family, especially valuable for committee-room gameplay; hearing rooms should not be copied from Russell or Hart.


Official source:
https://www.senate.gov/about/historic-buildings-spaces/office-buildings/dirksen-building.htm

Verified identity:
- First occupied in 1982; largest Senate office building, built for the computer/telecommunications era.
- Senator offices are two-story duplex suites with connecting rooms and movable partitions, explicitly designed for reconfiguration.
- The building has a 90-foot skylit central atrium and modern circulation identity radically different from Russell/Dirksen.
- The Central Hearing Facility was built for major high-interest proceedings with crowd, acoustics and television-camera needs in mind.


Base-art implication: contemporary/late-modern two-level office suites + dramatic atrium + large media-ready hearing family. Do not apply dark wood/classical detailing merely because it is Congress.


Official source:
https://www.senate.gov/about/historic-buildings-spaces/office-buildings/hart-building.htm

- 2026 ERA OVERRIDE: Governor’s current office address is 1021 O Street, Suite 9000; 1021 O Street is the Capitol Annex Swing Space used during the Capitol Annex project.
- Legislature: contemporary working offices are also affected by the Annex/swing-space program, while historic Capitol chambers/ceremonial spaces remain a separate visual family.
- Core asset logic: do NOT automatically use historic Capitol interiors for all 2026 working scenes.
- Classification: ERA/TEMPORARY OVERRIDE + HISTORIC CAPITOL + MODERN SWING-SPACE FAMILY.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING for actual 1021 O Street working interiors.

- Executive/legislature: Nebraska Capitol; unicameral legislature.
- Core asset logic: famous Art Deco skyscraper/tower statehouse plus unique unicameral chamber.
- Current exact governor room should be reverified before exact 2026 render if older map/Blue Book source is used.
- Classification: UNIQUE / MUST CUSTOMIZE.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING.

claims.locator: Texas — FUNCTIONAL ROOM DIFFERENTIATION CONFIRMED, VISUAL EXTRACTION CONTINUES
claims.statement:
Current official Capitol directory confirms distinct Governor spaces rather than one all-purpose office: Public Reception Room (Capitol 2S.1), Press Conference space (2S.2), Business Office (1S.1), and Legislative Division (1S.1), alongside chamber and Extension functions.
Production implication: executive scenes can select a real functional room family based on activity instead of teleporting every meeting, press event, bill negotiation and reception into one generic Governor office.
Photo-pack status: FUNCTION MAP STRONG; ROOM-SPECIFIC VISUAL PACK still incomplete.

- Capitol: ornate Capitol contains chambers and major ceremonial/executive spaces; State Reception Room historically/physically relates to Governor suite.
- Legislative working offices: rank-and-file legislators use the Capitol Annex, not ornate chambers as their normal office backdrop.
- Core asset logic: ornate Capitol/chamber/reception family + much more functional Annex office/committee family.
- Classification: STATE-SPECIFIC SPLIT CAMPUS.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING/partial.

- Executive: Governor/cabinet operate from Patrick Henry Building, not from a generic Capitol governor office.
- Legislature: chambers in historic Virginia Capitol.
- Member/staff offices: NEW General Assembly Building opened 2023; members/staff moved there from temporary Pocahontas space.
- Core asset logic: three clear families — Patrick Henry executive, historic Capitol chamber, contemporary General Assembly Building.
- Classification: UNIQUE MULTI-BUILDING CAMPUS / IMPORTANT CURRENT-ERA CHANGE.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING.

- Executive/chambers: Governor and House/Senate chambers in historic Tennessee State Capitol.
- Legislative member offices and committees: Cordell Hull Building; leadership/member suites distributed there.
- Core asset logic: historic Capitol for chamber/executive scenes + modern Cordell Hull working-office/committee family.
- Classification: STATE-SPECIFIC SPLIT CAMPUS.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING.

- Capitol: Governor/chambers use Minnesota State Capitol.
- Legislature: Minnesota Senate Building and State Office Building form additional working-office families.
- 2026 ERA FLAG: State Office Building construction/closure/renovation conditions materially affect normal occupancy; temporary space must be researched for selected date.
- Classification: STATE-SPECIFIC SPLIT CAMPUS + ERA OVERRIDE.
- Visual pack: PENDING.

- Governor spaces are functionally separate in official Capitol directory: Public Reception Room, Press Conference area, Business Office, Legislative Division.
- Legislature: historic Capitol plus underground Capitol Extension; representatives and committee staff can inhabit materially different office environments.
- Core asset logic: do not collapse governor into one room or legislature into one background.
- Classification: UNIQUE/STATE-SPECIFIC MULTI-FAMILY.
- Visual pack: PARTIAL; high-priority expansion.

- Executive: Governor Executive Chamber in State Capitol; official schedules/records identify Second Floor, Red Room and other Capitol executive spaces.
- Legislature: Assembly/Senate chambers in ornate Capitol; many member offices in Legislative Office Building.
- Core asset logic: extraordinary Capitol executive/chamber family + separate large LOB working-office family.
- Classification: UNIQUE CAPITOL + STATE-SPECIFIC LOB.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING.

- Executive/legislature: high-rise Art Deco State Capitol; official maps locate Governor and legislative chambers/leadership/committee spaces within complex.
- Core asset logic: skyscraper Capitol/Judicial Wing family.
- Classification: UNIQUE / MUST CUSTOMIZE.
- Visual pack: high priority PENDING.

- Roundhouse + Capitol North contain Governor, statewide officers, House/Senate and legislative offices/committee activity.
- Circular architecture and major New Mexico art identity are foundational, not decoration.
- Classification: UNIQUE / MUST CUSTOMIZE.
- Visual pack: PARTIAL; high-priority full pack.
